mAP@0.5 vs. mAP@0.5:0.95: What’s the Difference?
summary: mAP@0.5 uses a single 0.50 IoU threshold; mAP@0.5:0.95 averages ten thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95. See how each is calculated and when to use it.
body_text: Dikshant Shah Published Aug 14, 2026 • 14 min read SUMMARY mAP@0.5 evaluates detection at a single IoU threshold of 0.50, while mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluates it across ten thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, providing a stricter measure of a model’s detection and localization accuracy. This guide covers what these metrics mean, how they are calculated, and when to use them. When evaluating an object detection model , you will often see metrics such as mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 . Both measure how well a model detects objects, but they evaluate bounding box quality at different levels of strictness. The key difference is simple: mAP@0.5 evaluates predictions at a single IoU threshold of 0.50, while mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluates predictions across ten IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95 and averages the results. In this guide, we’ll break down the concepts behind mAP and IoU thresholds step by step: First, we’ll understand Precision and Recall. Then, we’ll look at Confidence Scores. Next, we’ll use these concepts to calculate Average Precision (AP). Then, we’ll see how AP is used to calculate Mean Average Precision (mAP) . Finally, we’ll introduce IoU thresholds and understand the difference between mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95. By the end, you’ll understand how these metrics are calculated, what they tell you about an object detection model, and when to use mAP@0.5 versus mAP@0.5:0.95. Understanding Precision and Recall What Is Precision? Precision measures how many of the model's positive predictions for a specific object class are correct. In object detection, a positive prediction means that the model has detected an object and assigned it to the target class. High precision means that the model's predictions for that class are usually correct, with relatively few false positives. A false positive (FP) occurs when the model predicts an object as belonging to a class, but the prediction does not correctly match a ground-truth object of that class. Low precision means that the model frequently makes incorrect detections for that class, resulting in more false positives. Precision is especially important when false positives are costly. For example, in a defect detection system, a false positive could cause a non-defective product to be incorrectly rejected. What Is Recall? Recall measures how many of the actual objects belonging to a specific class the model successfully detects. In object detection, an actual positive case means that an object of the target class is present in the ground-truth annotations. High recall means that the model detects most of the objects of a class that are actually present. Low recall means that the model misses many objects of that class, resulting in more false negatives. A false negative (FN) occurs when an object belonging to a specific class is present in the ground truth, but the model fails to detect it correctly. Recall is especially important when false negatives are costly. For example, in defect detection, missing a defective product could allow a faulty item to reach customers. How Are Precision and Recall Calculated? Precision and Recall are calculated using True Positives (TP), False Positives (FP), and False Negatives (FN). In object detection, these values are class-specific, meaning each object class has its own TP, FP, and FN counts. As a result, Precision and Recall are also class-specific. These values can be determined by comparing the model's predictions with the ground-truth annotations and organizing the results in a confusion matrix , as shown below. Confusion Matrix for an Object Detection Class Where: When a model correctly identifies an object as belonging to the positive class, it is a True Positive (TP). When the model predicts an object or class that is not actually present, it is a False Positive (FP). Similarly, a False Negative (FN) occurs when the model fails to detect an object that is actually present While a True Negative (TN) occurs when the model correctly identifies the absence of an object. You can then use the formula below to calculate the Precision: You can then use the formula below to calculate the Recall: In the above formulas, TP, FP, and FN represent the total number of True Positives, False Positives, and False Negatives, respectively for a specific class. True Negatives (TN) are generally not required to calculate Precision and Recall in object detection. Understanding Confidence Scores What Is a Confidence Score? A confidence score indicates how confident an object detection model is in a prediction, including the predicted object class and its location. Based on the confidence score, the researcher, developer, or engineer sets a confidence threshold to determine which predictions are accepted as detections and which are rejected. For example, an object detection model might return a prediction in JSON format like the following: { "class": "car", "confidence": 0.92, "bounding_box": { "x": 120, "y": 80, "width": 200, "height": 150 } } Example of an predicted car object How Does the Confidence Threshold Affect Precision and Recall? Changing the confidence threshold changes which predictions are accepted as detections, which in turn affects the model's Precision and Recall for a class. A higher threshold typically results in fewer, more confident detections, while a lower threshold allows more predictions to be accepted but may also introduce more false positives. For example, suppose an object detection model produces four predictions for the car class with confidence scores of 0.95, 0.85, 0.65, and 0.40. If the confidence threshold is set to 0.80, only the predictions with confidence scores of 0.95 and 0.85 are accepted. If the threshold is lowered to 0.50, the prediction with a confidence score of 0.65 is also accepted. In general: Higher confidence threshold -> generally higher precision, lower recall: Only the most confident predictions are accepted as detections. This can reduce false positives but may also cause the model to miss some actual objects. Lower confidence threshold -> generally lower precision, higher recall: More predictions are accepted as detections, which can help detect more actual objects but may also increase false positives. Therefore, there is usually a trade-off between Precision and Recall when selecting a confidence threshold. The best threshold depends on the application and whether it is more important to minimize false positives or minimize missed detections. Understanding Average Precision (AP) What Is a Precision-Recall Curve? As explained above, changing the confidence threshold changes the model's Precision and Recall for a class. By evaluating the model at different confidence thresholds, we can plot a Precision-Recall (PR) curve to visualize the relationship between Precision and Recall. Y-axis: Precision X-axis: Recall Precision-Recall Curve for a Class What Is Average Precision? Average Precision (AP) summarizes the Precision-Recall curve for an individual class into a single value by measuring the area under the curve (AUC). A higher AP indicates that the model maintains higher precision across different levels of recall, indicating better overall detection performance for that class. Calculating the AUC of the Precision-Recall Curve for a Class AP can be approximated by summing the areas of small rectangles under the Precision-Recall curve. Mathematically, this can be expressed using a discrete Riemann sum : Where: P(Ri) is the precision at the right endpoint of the i -th recall interval. Ri − Ri−1 is the width of the recall interval. n is the total number of recall intervals. Instead of selecting a single confidence threshold and reporting, "The model has 75% precision and 80% recall for this class," AP evaluates the model across multiple confidence thresholds, considers the resulting Precision-Recall relationship, and summarizes its overall performance for that class in a single value. Understanding Mean Average Precision (mAP) What Is mAP? Mean Average Precision (mAP) summarizes an object detection model's performance across all object classes by averaging their Average Precision (AP) values. The resulting score ranges from 0 to 1 and is often reported as a percentage. In other words, mAP is the mean of the Average Precision (AP) values across all detection classes in an object detection model. How Is mAP Calculated? Where: N is the total number of classes. APi is the Average Precision for class i . For example, consider an object detection model capable of detecting various types of vehicles, with: This means the model achieves an AP of 0.82 for the car class. Once the AP has been calculated for every class, we calculate mAP by taking the mean of the AP values across all classes: where (N) is the total number of detection classes. Understanding IoU and IoU Thresholds What Is Intersection over Union (IoU)? IoU (Intersection over Union) measures how much a predicted bounding box overlaps with the ground-truth bounding box. The formula is: It is commonly used to evaluate the localization accuracy of an object detection model. Localization refers to the model's ability to accurately determine where an object is located in an image by placing a bounding box around it. A model can correctly identify an object but still have poor localization if its predicted bounding box does not closely align with the actual object. The examples below demonstrate ground-truth bounding boxes (green) and predicted bounding boxes (other colors), along with their corresponding IoU values. Poor, Good, and Excellent Object Localization What Is an IoU Threshold? The IoU threshold is the minimum IoU value required for a prediction to be considered a correct detection (True Positive) . A lower IoU threshold is more forgiving, while a higher IoU threshold requires the predicted box to align more closely with the ground-truth box. For example, if the IoU threshold is 0.4: IoU ≥ 0.4 → prediction is considered a True Positive IoU < 0.4 → prediction is considered a False Positive What Is mAP@0.5? mAP@0.5 refers to calculating mean Average Precision (mAP) using a single IoU threshold of 0.5 . At an IoU threshold of 0.5, a predicted bounding box must have an IoU of at least 0.5 with the corresponding ground-truth bounding box to be considered a True Positive (TP). The IoU threshold determines whether a prediction is considered a TP or FP. Therefore, changing the IoU threshold can change the number of TPs, FPs, and FNs, which in turn affects Precision, Recall, AP, and ultimately mAP. Earlier, when we calculated AP and mAP, we did not explicitly specify an IoU threshold. The threshold could be 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, or any other value between 0 and 1. At that stage, we assumed that the TPs, FPs, and FNs had already been determined based on a chosen IoU threshold. To indicate the IoU threshold used to calculate mAP, the threshold is specified after the “@” symbol. For example: mAP@0.5 uses an IoU threshold of 0.50. mAP@0.75 uses an IoU threshold of 0.75. mAP@0.5 is also commonly denoted as mAP50 or mAP@50 . How Is mAP@0.5 Calculated? mAP@0.5 is calculated by first calculating AP for each class using a single IoU threshold of 0.50, then averaging the AP values across all classes. Where: N is the total number of classes. APi@0.5 is the Average Precision for class i at an IoU threshold of 0.5. For example, for a vehicle detection model the mAP@0.5 would be calculated as shown below: What Does mAP@0.5 Tell You? mAP@0.5 tells us “How well does the model detect objects when we require at least 50% overlap between the predicted and ground-truth bounding boxes?” Because an IoU threshold of 0.5 is relatively forgiving, a prediction does not need to align extremely closely with the ground-truth bounding box to be considered correct. This makes mAP@0.5 useful for evaluating a model's overall object detection performance when approximate bounding-box localization is sufficient. What Is mAP@0.5:0.95? mAP@0.5:0.95 is the mean of the mAP values calculated at 10 different IoU thresholds , ranging from 0.50 to 0.95 in increments of 0.05. Unlike mAP@0.5, which evaluates the model using only a single IoU threshold of 0.50, mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluates the model across multiple IoU thresholds. This provides a stricter assessment of both object detection and bounding-box localization accuracy. The 10 IoU thresholds are: 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90, and 0.95. mAP@0.5:0.95 is also commonly denoted as mAP50-95 or mAP@50:95 . How Is mAP@0.5:0.95 Calculated? At each of the 10 IoU thresholds, mAP is calculated separately. The resulting 10 mAP values are then averaged to obtain the final mAP@0.5:0.95 score. Equivalently, Why Is mAP@0.5:0.95 Usually Lower Than mAP@0.5? mAP@0.5:0.95 is usually lower than mAP@0.5 because it averages AP across increasingly strict IoU thresholds. As the IoU threshold increases, fewer predictions meet the required overlap with the ground-truth boxes to be considered True Positives. Consequently, AP generally decreases at higher IoU thresholds because predictions that would have been considered correct at a lower threshold may no longer qualify as True Positives. These lower AP values at stricter thresholds reduce the overall average, making mAP@0.5:0.95 a more demanding measure of both object detection performance and bounding-box localization accuracy. When Should You Use mAP@0.5 vs. mAP@0.5:0.95? The choice between these metrics depends on which aspect of object detection performance you want to evaluate. When Should You Use mAP@0.5? You want a simple measure of detection performance. Approximate bounding box localization is sufficient. Your application prioritizes detecting objects over precise localization. You want to evaluate whether a model is making generally correct detections. mAP@0.5 is useful for assessing whether a model can detect objects with reasonably accurate bounding boxes, but it does not provide a complete picture of localization quality. In simple terms, mAP@0.5 answers: “Can the model detect the object with a reasonably accurate bounding box?” When Should You Use mAP@0.5:0.95? You want a more comprehensive evaluation of detection performance. Precise bounding box localization is important. You are comparing modern object detection models. You want to evaluate your model using the COCO evaluation protocol. Because mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluates performance across multiple IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, it is generally a more informative metric for assessing overall object detection performance. In simple terms, mAP@0.5:0.95 answers: “Can the model detect the object and consistently localize it precisely?” How to Get mAP Values from Roboflow Train Roboflow Train is a model training platform by Roboflow that lets you train computer vision models on your annotated datasets without the need to manage complex training infrastructure or write training code. Learn how to train an object detection model. Roboflow Train supports training computer vision models for tasks such as object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, classification, and keypoint detection. With Roboflow Train, you can: Upload and version datasets Apply preprocessing and augmentations to entire datasets Train state-of-the-art models Evaluate model performance Deploy models for inference When you train an object detection model using Roboflow Train, it reports key mAP metrics, including mAP@0.5, mAP@0.75, and mAP@0.5:0.95. mAP metrics at different IoU thresholds for a construction safety model trained in Roboflow. Roboflow provides mAP@0.5:0.95, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.75 across All , Small , Medium , and Large object sizes to provide a more detailed evaluation of object detection performance. In Roboflow, Small, Medium, and Large refer to the size of an object's ground-truth bounding box, measured by its area in pixels. These categories follow the COCO evaluation convention: Small: Bounding-box area is less than 1,024 pixels². Medium: Bounding-box area is between 1,024 and 9,216 pixels². Large: Bounding-box area is greater than 9,216 pixels². These categories help you understand how well a model performs when detecting objects of different sizes. Small objects occupy a relatively small area of the image, such as a distant person or a tiny defect. Medium objects occupy a moderate area, while large objects occupy a relatively large area of the image, such as a nearby person or vehicle. For example, if a model achieves mAP@0.5 of 45% for Small objects, 72% for Medium objects, and 89% for Large objects, this indicates that the model performs substantially better when detecting large objects than small objects. It is important to note that these categories are based on the absolute pixel area of the bounding box , not the object's physical size or its relative size within the image. This is particularly important for high-resolution images. An object may appear relatively small compared with the overall image but still have a large bounding box in terms of pixels and therefore be classified as a Large object. You can also use Roboflow Agent to access these evaluation metrics for a model you have trained in Roboflow. Roboflow Agent provides a conversational interface for interacting with Roboflow tools, including Roboflow Train, Roboflow Deploy, and Roboflow Workflows. How to Calculate mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 on Your Dataset You can calculate mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 on your own dataset using a trained object detection model with Supervision . In the example below, we calculate both metrics for a fine-tuned RF-DETR Small model using a dataset in COCO format. First, install the required Python packages: pip install supervision rfdetr pillow Then, run the following script: import supervision as sv from rfdetr import RFDETRSmall from PIL import Image # Load the RF-DETR Small model with the trained weights model = RFDETRSmall( pretrain_weights=r"weights.pt", # Use Absolute Path Here ) # Benchmark the model on the test dataset mean_average_precision = sv.MeanAveragePrecision.benchmark( # Load the test dataset from COCO-format annotations dataset=sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco( images_directory_path="dataset/test", annotations_path="dataset/test/_annotations.coco.json" ), # Define how the model makes predictions for each test image callback=lambda image: model.predict( Image.fromarray(image), ) ) # Print mAP at IoU = 0.50 print(f"mAP50: {mean_average_precision.map50:.3f}") # Print mAP averaged across IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95 print(f"mAP50:95: {mean_average_precision.map50_95:.3f}") You can also use the same benchmarking approach with other object detection models, such as YOLO , as long as the model's prediction output can be converted to the format expected by supervision. Simply replace the RF-DETR model and its prediction function in the callback with the corresponding model and inference method. This allows you to use the same test dataset and evaluation procedure to compare the performance of different object detection models using mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95. Conclusion: mAP@0.5 vs. mAP@0.5:0.95 mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 are both useful metrics for evaluating object detection models, but they measure performance at different levels of localization strictness. While mAP@0.5 evaluates the model at a single IoU threshold of 0.50, mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluates it across ten thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95. As a result, mAP@0.5 is useful for understanding general detection performance, while mAP@0.5:0.95 provides a more comprehensive view of both detection and localization accuracy. Roboflow Train makes this evaluation easier by automatically calculating and reporting these mAP metrics during model training, allowing you to quickly assess how well your trained model performs at different IoU thresholds. title: VA loan vs FHA: key insights to make the right choice
summary: Compare VA loan vs FHA to see eligibility, down payment rules, pros, cons, and more. Learn which mortgage option works best for your homebuying needs.
body_text: If you’re a first-time homebuyer considering a VA loan vs FHA loan, you may wonder which loan is right for you. Both home loans are a popular option for first-time buyers. You must be a military member, veteran, or a surviving spouse to qualify for a VA loan. Meanwhile, FHA loans are available to any borrower who meets the eligibility requirements. We'll explain the key differences between a VA loan vs FHA loan so you know what to expect. See your homebuying budget ...in as little as 3 minutes – no credit impact VA vs FHA loans What are FHA and VA loans? They're government-backed home loans that can provide a more affordable path to homeownership. Government-insured loans like VA and FHA loans are less risky for lenders. That means they typically offer more competitive rates and loan terms, and less stringent credit requirements. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs insures VA loans . Two standout features of VA loans are that they don't require a down payment or mortgage insurance fees. Meanwhile, FHA loans are insured by the Federal Housing Administration. These loans have lower minimum credit scoreand down payment requirements than conventional loans. Better offers FHA loans and VA loans with competitive rates and provides a simple application process. Eligibility VA loan vs FHA loan eligibility requirements differ. FHA loans are accessible to any buyer who meets the credit score, DTI ratio, and down payment requirements. VA loans are more restrictive. To be eligible for a VA loan, you must be an active-duty military member, veteran, or surviving military spouse. Down payment FHA loans require borrowers to make a down payment of at least 3.5%. For those with a credit score of 580 or higher, the minimum down payment is 3.5% of the home’s purchase price. Those with credit scores between 500 and 579 must make a 10% down payment. For most borrowers, there are no minimum down payment requirements for a VA loan. Credit score The minimum credit score for an FHA loan is 500 . There’s no official minimum credit score needed to qualify for a VA loan. However, most lenders require a credit score of at least 620. Interest rates Since FHA loans and VA loans are government-insured home loans, lenders tend to offer more competitive interest ratesand loan terms compared to conventional home loans. Remember: your financial situation and credit score can influence the interest rate you qualify for when applying for a home loan. Related: Current VA loan rates Property type Both loans are intended to finance a primary residence where the borrower lives. This can include a single-family home, a multi-family property (up to four units), a manufactured home, or new construction home. VA and FHA loans have strict property standards to ensure that a home is safe, secure, and structurally sound. For an FHA loan, the property must meet minimum standards set by the Department of Housing and Urban Development. For a VA loan, the property must meet the minimum requirements set by the Department of Veterans Affairs. Debt-to-income (DTI) ratio Many lenders require FHA loan applicants to have a DTI of 43% or less. But lenders may approve an applicant with a DTI above 43% in some cases. At Better Mortgage, there are circumstances where a DTI ratio of up to 57% is allowed . The VA suggests an ideal DTI ratio of 41% or less for VA loans. If you have a higher DTI, you'll face more scrutiny during the application process. Closing costs FHA loan borrowers can generally expect to pay closing costs totaling between 2% to 6% of the home’s purchase price. VA loan borrowers should also prepare to pay closing costs, which typically range from 3% to 6% of the home’s purchase price. Loan limits FHA loan limits vary by location. For 2025, the loan limits are $524,225 for borrowers in most counties and $1,209,750 for borrowers in high-cost counties. There are no VA loan limits for veterans with full entitlement. For borrowers with partial entitlement, county-based loan limits may apply. Mortgage insurance and fees FHA loan borrowers pay an upfront mortgage insurance premium (UFMIP) and annual mortgage insurance premiums(MIPS). A UFMIP of 1.75% of the loan amount, is paid at closing or rolled into the loan amount. Meanwhile, annual MIPs are included in your monthly mortgage payment. Factors like the down payment amount, loan-to-value ratio, and loan amount influence your annual MIPs. But you can expect to pay anywhere from 0.15% to 0.75% of the loan amount each year. VA loans don't require borrowers to pay private mortgage insurance (PMI) or other ongoing mortgage insurance. However, borrowers must pay a one-time VA funding fee, ranging from 1.25% to 3.3% of the loan amount, at closing. This fee can be financed into the loan. See your homebuying budget ...in as little as 3 minutes – no credit impact Refinancing VA and FHA loans VA loans and FHA loans can be refinanced. Since these home loans are government-backed, they qualify for a streamlined refinancing process, which can reduce paperwork and result in faster processing. You can streamline refinance an existing FHA loan into a new FHA loan or streamline refinance an existing VA loan into a new VA loan. Alternatively, borrowers can refinance a VA loan or FHA loan to a conventional loan. You must meet eligibilityrequirements for the new loan and lender. VA loan vs. FHA loan pros and cons Is a VA loan better than an FHA loan? To decide whether a VA loan or FHA loan is best for you, it’s beneficial to consider the advantages and disadvantages of each loan type. Let’s review some of the top pros and cons. Pros and cons of VA loans Here are some VA loan pros and cons to consider: Pros Cons No down payment for most borrowers Must pay VA funding fee No private mortgage insurance Strict property standards and appraisal requirements Tend to have lower interest rates Extended closing time No loan limits for most borrowers Pros and cons of FHA loans Here are some FHA loan pros and cons to consider: Pros Cons Lower credit score requirements than conventional loans Must pay upfront and annual mortgage insurance premiums Low minimum down payment requirements Limitations on borrowing amounts May be easier to qualify compared to a conventional loan Strict property standards and appraisal requirements Less strict DTI ratio requirements Extended closing times Choosing between FHA and VA loans Still unsure whether a VA vs FHA loan is right for you? Your ideal home loan will depend on your financial situation and needs. If you're eligible, a VA loan may be the best fit. Perks like no down payment and no mortgage insurance could provide significant savings. An FHA loan may be ideal if you have a low credit score or are building your credit. Before deciding between VA vs. FHA loans, shop around and compare loan options. Better can help you compare VA vs FHA loan options. VA vs FHA loan FAQs Is a VA or an FHA loan a better option for a first-time homebuyer? A VA loan or FHA loan can be an excellent option for first-time homebuyers. However, your personal situation and finances will determine which home loan option is the best fit for you. An FHA loan may be a more ideal option for someone working to build their credit. A VA loan may be a suitable option for individuals struggling to save for a down payment. Why might a seller decline an FHA or VA loan? A seller might decline an offer from a buyer with an FHA or VA loan due to stricter property and appraisal requirements, as well as the potential for repairs needed to close and longer closing times. Conclusion For eligible borrowers, VA loans and FHA loans can make homebuying more affordable. For active-duty military members and veterans, a VA loan offers benefits such as $0 down payment , no mortgage insurance premiums, and favorable interest rates. FHA loans are also an attractive home loan option to explore due to low minimum credit score requirements, low minimum down payment requirements, and competitive interest rates. Better offers tools that make it easy to compare FHA vs. VA loans fast, check $0-down VA options, and lock in a rate. See your homebuying budget ...in as little as 3 minutes – no credit impact

title: Imagine a chemist from 1950 walking into a modern pharmaceutical R&D lab.
summary: Read the latest news and updates from ReactWise about AI-driven chemistry and process optimization.
body_text: Imagine a chemist from 1950 walking into a modern pharmaceutical R&D lab. The first thing that would stop them in their tracks might not be the robots or the screens. It would be the notebooks. Or rather - the absence of them. In 1950, a chemist's notebook was sacred. Every observation recorded. Every anomaly noted. The color of the precipitate. The smell before and after addition. The exact sequence of every step. Because they understood that chemistry lives in the details, and details forgotten are experiments wasted. Walk into many labs today and you'll find something different. Terabytes of analytical data. Thousands of HPLC traces. Hundreds of optimization runs. But sometimes none of the contextual observations that would tell you what was actually happening. We got faster. We got more data than any generation of chemists in history. And somewhere along the way, we stopped writing things down. It's not that chemists stopped caring. It's that the tools rewarded speed over context, and nobody built a place for the observation to go. The irony is that everything that made those old lab notebooks so valuable - the narrative, the context, the human observation - is exactly what modern AI needs to be truly powerful. The order of addition. The lot number of the catalyst. The note that says "mixture turned slightly yellow upon addition." That sentence carries more chemical meaning than most datasets ever capture. The chemists who built this industry knew that today's observation is tomorrow's insight. At @ReactWise, we're building the infrastructure to make sure that knowledge never gets lost again - and can be used for understanding chemistry better. The best of what came before. Powered by what's possible now. ‍

title: Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports full fine-tuning
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports full fine-tuning
body_text: Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports full fine-tuning for over 25 open-source models. These include popular models from gpt-oss, Gemma, Llama, Nemotron, and Qwen model families. In addition to parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA, which update a small subset of model weights, you can now update all parameters in the model for deeper adaptation when your use case requires it. Full fine-tuning allows the model to more thoroughly learn your domain-specific patterns, terminology, and task structure. This is particularly valuable when you need the model to acquire capabilities beyond surface-level style adjustments, such as learning specialized reasoning patterns, adopting complex output formats, or internalizing domain knowledge from large proprietary datasets. With serverless model customization, SageMaker manages all infrastructure provisioning and training orchestration, so you can run full fine-tuning jobs without provisioning or managing any infrastructure and you pay only for what you use. Serverless full fine-tuning on SageMaker is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To get started, navigate to the JumpStart and Models page in Amazon SageMaker Studio to launch a customization job, or use the SageMaker Python SDK . To learn more, and see the supported list of models, see the Amazon SageMaker AI model customization documentation.

title: ’65 Mustang Pace Car Edition Seeks Another 44 Years of Loving Ownership
summary: While it’s standard practice to refer to early builds of Ford’s iconic 1965 Mustang as 1964.5 models, that’s technically not true. There’s a “5” in the VIN to exclaim to all observers that these Mustangs are, in fact, of the 1965 model year. But there’s just something about the 1965 Mustang Pace Car, as it […]
body_text: While it’s standard practice to refer to early builds of Ford’s iconic 1965 Mustang as 1964.5 models, that’s technically not true. There’s a “5” in the VIN to exclaim to all observers that these Mustangs are, in fact, of the 1965 model year. But there’s just something about the 1965 Mustang Pace Car, as it paced the Indianapolis 500 on one fine Saturday in May of 1964. There were 35 new Mustang convertibles at this race, but Ford made 190 hardtop replicas available for dealership retail sales. The Mustang pacing the Indy 500 was a huge moment, both for the model and for Ford Motor Company, and that moment, unfortunately, occurred in 1964. So the allure of a 1964 “and a half” Mustang continues apace. Each of the 190 replicas was finished in Pace Car white with blue interior trim and the F-code small-block V-8 engine. There were unique body side decals, and specific identification codes under the hood. The latter were made by a grease pencil on the radiator’s core support, and the seller of this particular example on Hagerty Marketplace ensured that what remains of those markings wasn’t lost in this Mustang’s sympathetic restoration. Body side decals matching those of the official Pace Car were applied, and the hood/roof/trunk had three blue racing stripes along their centerlines. The commemorative Pace Car coupes left the factory with grease pencil codes on that radiator core support, including the words “PACE CAR” for posterity. Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes This particular Pace Car Edition is unit #41, and was also used as a promotional vehicle at the Indy 500. It has remained with its current owner for 44 years, who purchased it back in 1982 as “just a basic white Mustang.” But it became much, much more after that owner researched the paint code and commissioned a forensic etching of the radiator core support. Turns out the original owner was in Missouri, and this Pace Car Edition was his high school graduation present. Delivery was delayed because of the Mustang’s use at Indianapolis, where it was dented and repaired without its trademark body side decals. Each subsequent owner was ignorant of this Mustang’s true provenance until it was time for a proper restoration. This Mustang Pace Car Edition has its original floors, trunk, doors, and engine compartment sheetmetal. Only the passenger-side quarter panel has evidence of repair from its tenure at the Indianapolis 500. An extensive restoration started in the 1980s, when the motor was rebuilt and the correct paint and graphics applied. By 2008, the Pace Car Edition had a rebuilt transmission, and a refreshed carburetor arrived in 2020. Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes Hagerty Marketplace | Classic-Tunes While this is an older restoration that shows modest signs of its age, a treasure trove of documentation is included with the sale, pointing to a delightful tale of redemption for what was once a courtesy vehicle at “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.” This Pace Car Edition lost its identifying decals shortly after the checkered flag flew at Indy in 1964, but today we are immensely grateful for what became of this now-temporary setback. As of this writing, there were 12 days left on the auction, with a high bid of $12,000 . Back in 2020, a 1965 Pace Car Edition sold for a little over $20,000 on Bring a Trailer , but the overall market for 1965 Mustang Coupes has been stronger as of late. Perhaps we will see if provenance and a fantastic story of redemption will have an effect on the final outcome. The post ’65 Mustang Pace Car Edition Seeks Another 44 Years of Loving Ownership appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Adobe MAX 2026: Travel guide for Miami Beach
summary: : Plan your Adobe MAX 2026 trip to Miami Beach with tips for hotels, flights, airport transfers, budgeting, packing, dining, and the MAX agenda.
body_text: Adobe MAX 2026 brings designers, creative leaders, photographers, video professionals, marketers, and other creatives to Miami Beach for three days of keynotes, sessions, hands-on labs, Creative Park, and networking.[1] With popular sessions and labs requiring advance scheduling, hotel options spread across Miami Beach, and major events like MAX Sneaks and MAX Bash competing for time, planning ahead can help you get more from the conference and bring useful ideas and new skills back to your team. What is Adobe MAX and who is it for? Adobe MAX is Adobe's flagship creativity conference, bringing designers, creative directors, marketers, photographers, video professionals, and other creatives together for keynotes, sessions, hands-on labs, MAX Sneaks, Creative Park, and networking.[1] The 2026 in-person event is at the Miami Beach Convention Center and offers optional preconference courses Nov. 8–9 with the main event taking place Nov. 10–12.[1][2] The program includes more than 200 sessions and labs across seven tracks covering topics such as AI, branding, creative leadership, the creator economy, design and illustration, photography, and video and motion.[1][4] Attendees can also take part in photowalks, explore Adobe products and partner technologies in Creative Park, and attend evening events including the Welcome Reception and MAX Bash.[1][4] If you're trying to get buy-in to attend, identify the most relevant skills, tools, and ideas you can walk away with. Prioritize hands-on labs and sessions that support your current projects, make time to explore new workflows and technologies in Creative Park, and look for opportunities to connect with other creative professionals facing similar challenges. What makes Adobe MAX 2026 worth the trip Adobe MAX combines product announcements and previews with hands-on learning, access to Adobe experts, and opportunities to connect with other creative professionals. Keynotes and MAX Sneaks offer a look at what Adobe is developing, while sessions and labs give attendees opportunities to build skills across AI, branding, creative leadership, design, photography, video, and other areas.[1][3][4] Plan around these in-person experiences: Keynotes and MAX Sneaks: Hear Adobe announcements and see experimental technologies and projects from Adobe Labs.[1][3][4] Hands-on labs and photowalks: Build practical skills in 90-minute labs using MAX-provided equipment or join two-hour photography experiences around Miami Beach.[4] Creative Park: Meet Adobe experts, explore sponsor demonstrations and activations, and attend Creative Park theater programming between sessions.[1][4] Welcome Reception and MAX Bash: Make time for two of the conference's major evening events and additional opportunities to connect with other attendees.[3] Preconference courses and certification: Add a full-day course before MAX or take one complimentary Adobe Certified Professional exam during conference week.[1][3][4] What you learn at MAX doesn't have to stay in Miami Beach. Focus your schedule on sessions, labs, and conversations that can inform your current projects, introduce new tools or workflows, and give you practical ideas to share with your team when you return. Where to stay for Adobe MAX 2026 Where you stay can shape how much time you spend getting to sessions, whether you can return to your room between activities, and how easily you get back after evening events like MAX Bash. Adobe offers an official hotel block across Miami Beach, including properties within walking distance of the Miami Beach Convention Center and others with MAX shuttle service.[17] Hotels by distance to Miami Beach Convention Center Compare hotel areas by convention center access, transportation, and typical pricing: Area MBCC access Details Rates Convention Center/Central South Beach Walk Closest to MBCC, with several official MAX hotels within walking distance High South Beach Walk or short rideshare Larger selection of hotels, restaurants, and nightlife; some official MAX properties are considered walkable Moderate to high Mid-Beach/Collins Avenue MAX shuttle or rideshare Official MAX hotels farther from MBCC may offer conference shuttle service Moderate to high If you expect early sessions, labs throughout the day, or a packed agenda, staying within walking distance of MBCC can simplify the week. Hotels farther north along Collins Avenue can offer more options while still connecting you to the convention center through official MAX shuttle service. If you book outside the MAX hotel block, check your transportation options and travel time before confirming your stay. Adobe MAX hotel pricing Navan looked at anonymized October hotel booking patterns during Adobe MAX 2024 in Miami Beach to provide context for hotel pricing.[13] Use these benchmarks while planning your trip: Median hotel rate: During conference week, the median nightly rate near the event venue was $378, roughly 6% higher than a typical October week in Miami Beach ($356 median).[13] Stay length: Business travelers stayed an average of 2.7 nights at 4.1-star hotels.[13] Late bookings: Roughly 57% of bookings were made within two weeks of check-in, including nearly 32% during the final week before arrival.[13] Adobe offers negotiated rates at official MAX hotels across Miami Beach, with the 2026 hotel block available through Oct. 16 or until rooms sell out.[17] If you're booking through Adobe's official MAX hotel program, keep these points in mind: Book through MAX: Negotiated hotel rates are available through MAX registration or the Attendee Dashboard rather than by contacting hotels directly.[17] Watch the deadline: MAX hotel rates are available through Oct. 16, 2026, or until rooms sell out.[17] Check transportation: Some official hotels are within walking distance of MBCC, while properties farther away offer MAX shuttle service.[17] Compare the full stay cost: Resort fees, parking charges, and cancellation terms vary by property.[17] Adobe MAX flight trends Miami International Airport (MIA) is the primary airport serving Miami Beach.[8][9] Navan flight data from MAX week 2024 shows 295 business flights into Miami, with 21.7% from international origins.[13] The most common origin cities were New York, Atlanta, London, San Francisco, and Newark, with additional volume from Phoenix, Los Angeles, and Boston.[13] If you're attending the main conference, consider arriving Monday, Nov. 9, so you have time to get to Miami Beach and settle in before Tuesday's programming begins. If you're attending a preconference course Nov. 8 or Nov. 9, plan your arrival around your course schedule instead. How Navan Edge helps you book your conference travel Use Navan Edge, your travel assistant powered by AI and 24/7 human travel experts, to plan and book your Adobe MAX trip. Compare flights, hotels, and restaurants using live availability, personal preferences, and all the amenities that are important to you , then book everything in the same thread without juggling multiple apps or websites. If you need help along the way, a human travel expert is available 24/7 and can help from wherever you left off in the booking process. Continue earning your usual airline miles and hotel loyalty points, get your credit card points, and earn an additional 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays. See our travel rewards on business trips guide for how it works. How to budget for conference travel to Miami Beach Your Adobe MAX travel budget should account for the full cost of the trip, from registration and lodging to transportation, meals, and other expenses. Planning for those costs upfront can help you set a realistic budget before requesting approval. Federal per diem for Miami Beach The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) sets federal per diem rates by city and season. At the time of publication, GSA had not yet published FY2027 rates, which will apply to Adobe MAX 2026. For planning purposes, FY2026 Miami-Dade County rates were: $237 per day combined: Includes $145 for nightly lodging plus $92 for daily meals and incidental expenses (M&IE)[7] M&IE breakdown: Includes $23 for breakfast, $26 for lunch, $38 for dinner, and $5 for incidentals (reduce your meal allowance for any catering at the event)[7] First and last travel days: Includes an M&IE allowance of $69 (i.e., 75% of the daily M&IE rate)[7] Updated rates for FY2027 (October 2026–September 2027) are expected to be published in mid-August 2026 at gsa.gov. Other expenses to consider Planning for these expenses before you book can make it easier to stay within budget, secure travel approval, and avoid surprises when it's time to submit your expense report. Conference registration: A full conference pass costs $1,795 through Sept. 15, with standard registration increasing to $1,995 afterward. Check the event website for official rates and pricing tiers.[5] Preconference courses: Optional full-day courses on Nov. 8–9 are priced separately from the full conference pass.[3] Conference meals: Full conference registration includes breakfast and lunch Tuesday through Thursday, so adjust your M&IE reimbursement accordingly.[3] Airport transfer: The Miami Beach Airport Express costs $2.25 each way, while rideshare fares vary based on traffic and demand.[8][9] Client dinners: Private dining and upscale restaurants in Miami Beach typically cost $75–$150 per person. After-hours networking: Leave room in your budget for team dinners, partner-hosted gatherings, and other events beyond official MAX programming. Plan your Adobe MAX agenda With more than 200 sessions and labs on the MAX schedule, deciding what not to attend can be just as important as choosing what makes your list.[4] Start with your highest-priority sessions and hands-on labs, then leave room for Creative Park, photowalks, and conversations with other attendees. Adobe has published the schedule on the official MAX 2026 in-person agenda. Registration opens on Tuesday at 8 a.m., and here is a quick look at the overall day-by-day calendar:[4] Sunday–Monday (Nov. 8–9): Optional preconference courses[4] Monday–Thursday (Nov. 9–12): Adobe Certified Professional exams[4] Tuesday (Nov. 10): Day One Keynote, sessions, labs, photowalks, Creative Park, and the Welcome Reception[3][4] Wednesday (Nov. 11): Day Two Keynote, sessions, labs, photowalks, Creative Park, MAX Sneaks, and MAX Bash[3][4] Thursday (Nov. 12): Labs, photowalks, Creative Park, and the final session ending at 3 p.m.[4] Build flexibility into your schedule Add your highest-priority sessions and labs to your MAX schedule first, particularly hands-on experiences with limited capacity. Full conference attendees can initially schedule up to three labs and one photowalk, with the lab limit potentially lifted three weeks before MAX if space remains.[3] Keep these priorities in mind as you build your schedule: Sessions and labs: Prioritize the topics and hands-on learning opportunities most relevant to your work, and add limited-capacity sessions early.[3][4] Creative Park: Set aside time to meet Adobe experts, explore product demonstrations and sponsor activations, and attend Creative Park theater programming.[3][4] Keynotes and MAX Sneaks: Plan around major stage programming before filling the rest of your schedule with sessions and labs.[3][4] Logistics: Check your schedule and session locations throughout the day so you have enough time to move between activities. Our business trip planning guide covers general flight, hotel, and other travel planning beyond this MAX-specific checklist. What to pack and wear at Adobe MAX Adobe MAX doesn't require formal business attire, so comfortable, polished casual clothing works well for most conference days. Pack breathable clothes for warm Miami Beach weather, comfortable shoes for long days at MBCC, and a light layer for air-conditioned session rooms. If you have client dinners or other business meetings planned, bring an outfit that works for those occasions as well. Miami Beach is typically warm in November, with daytime highs around 80°F and overnight lows around 70°F.[6] November is also drier than the summer months, although rain is still possible.[6] You'll likely move between warm, humid conditions outdoors and cooler conference spaces throughout the day, so lightweight layers are useful. Conference essentials A few practical extras can make long conference days more comfortable, from navigating Miami's warm weather and cool session rooms to staying prepared during November cold and flu season. Add these essentials to your packing list: Two pairs of comfortable shoes: Alternate pairs during the conference to give your feet a break after long days at MBCC and walking around Miami Beach. Portable charger: Using the MAX schedule, messaging, maps, and other apps throughout the day can drain your battery. Reusable water bottle: Keep water with you during long stretches of sessions, labs, and Creative Park. Light sweater or jacket: Bring an extra layer for air-conditioned keynotes, labs, and session rooms. Compact umbrella or light rain jacket: November is relatively dry in Miami Beach, but showers are still possible. Snacks: Keep a protein bar or another easy snack in your bag in case sessions or labs overlap with your usual meal times. Hand sanitizer and cough drops: Keep both in your day bag for long days in crowded conference spaces. Earplugs: Pack a pair if you're a light sleeper, especially if your hotel is near South Beach nightlife. Getting from the airport to the Miami Beach Convention Center Rideshare or taxi is generally the simplest door-to-door option for travelers heading to Miami Beach from MIA, especially if you're arriving late, carrying extra gear, or staying away from a convenient transit stop. The Route 150 Miami Beach Airport Express costs considerably less and can work well if you're traveling light and have more time for the trip.[8][9] Option Time Cost Notes Route 150 Miami Beach Airport Express Varies $2.25 one way[9][10] Take the free MIA Mover to Miami International Airport Station, then connect to the bus for Miami Beach; travel time depends on traffic[8][9] Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) Roughly 26 minutes[16] $32[16] Uber reports historical averages of 26 minutes and $32 from MIA to MBCC; actual fares and travel times vary[16] Taxi Varies with traffic Metered fare Taxis depart from MIA's arrivals level; a $2 airport origination fee applies in addition to the metered fare[8] Beyond sessions: Make time for Creative Park and networking Some of the most useful parts of Adobe MAX happen outside scheduled sessions and labs. Leave time in your agenda for Creative Park, conversations with Adobe experts and other attendees, and networking events instead of filling every hour with scheduled programming. Schedule meetings before you arrive: Reach out to colleagues, partners, and other attendees you want to meet about two weeks before MAX to arrange a coffee or time to connect at Creative Park. Leave time for Creative Park: Set aside dedicated time to meet Adobe experts, explore sponsor demonstrations and activations, and attend Creative Park theater programming rather than squeezing it between sessions. Make room for evening events: The Welcome Reception and MAX Bash offer additional opportunities to meet other attendees outside the conference's daytime programming. Take notes after conversations: Jot down useful ideas, resources, and next steps while the details are still fresh. Follow up within 48 hours: Send a short email or LinkedIn message with a clear next step, whether that's sharing a resource, continuing a conversation, or making an introduction. Build in short breaks: Long days of sessions, labs, Creative Park, and walking around Miami Beach can be tiring. Leave enough space in your schedule to grab water, have a snack, or take a short break before your next activity. The best networking starts before you arrive and continues after you leave. Focus on conversations that connect to your work and interests, and make a note of any follow-up you want to make before moving on to your next session. A few useful conversations you continue after MAX can be more valuable than trying to meet as many people as possible. What to eat at Adobe MAX 2026 Full conference registration includes breakfast and lunch Tuesday through Thursday, so you won't need to plan every meal during MAX.[3] Remember to adjust your M&IE reimbursement for conference-provided meals, and keep a snack in your bag in case sessions or labs overlap with your usual meal times. For client dinners, team meals, or a chance to explore Miami Beach beyond conference catering, consider these options: Upscale dinner: Stubborn Seed offers a Michelin-starred tasting menu and private dining options for corporate and group events.[11] Team or group dinner: LT Steak & Seafood at The Betsy serves steaks and seafood and offers semi-private dining for groups.[12] Casual meal: Puerto Sagua Restaurant is a longtime South Beach spot for Cuban dishes, sandwiches, and coffee.[15] Close to MBCC: Rum Room Restaurant & Venu serves contemporary Latin-inspired dishes on the Miami Beach Convention Center campus, with private event space available for groups.[14] Navan Edge can also help you find and reserve Miami Beach restaurants in the same chat where you booked your flight and hotel. Finish strong on departure day A little preparation the night before departure can make your final MAX day easier, especially if you're checking out before Thursday's programming ends. Pack the night before: Set aside your travel clothes, charge your devices, and check the room for chargers, adapters, and other easy-to-miss items. Ask about late checkout: If you have an afternoon or evening flight, check with your hotel about late checkout or luggage storage so you don't have to carry your bags through the final day. Allow enough time at MIA: Plan to arrive at least two hours before a domestic flight and three hours before an international flight, and leave extra time for traffic between Miami Beach and the airport.[8] File expenses promptly: Upload receipts and note any expenses that require additional documentation while the details are still fresh. Use airport downtime: If you have lounge access or time before boarding, use it to organize notes, receipts, and follow-up tasks. Plan your follow-up: Set aside time after the conference to share useful takeaways with your team and reconnect with people you met at MAX. Make your Adobe MAX 2026 trip count A successful Adobe MAX trip starts with a little planning. Choose a hotel that makes it easy to get to MBCC, set a realistic budget, build your schedule around your highest-priority sessions and labs, and leave room for Creative Park, MAX Sneaks, and conversations with other attendees. Before you head home, organize your notes and follow-ups so you can bring useful ideas and new skills back to your team. Planning your Adobe MAX 2026 trip? title: Application Lifecycle Management: From Development to Deployment
summary: See how connected workflows help teams plan smarter, reduce handoff friction, and push releases with greater confidence.
body_text: By Morgan Dingle | Aug 17, 2026 Picture this: Your development team just spent six months building a groundbreaking application. The code is elegant, the features are innovative, and everyone’s excited for launch day. But then reality hits—deployment fails, integration issues emerge, and what should have been a triumph becomes a scramble. Sound familiar? Likewise, the difference between software success and failure often isn’t the code itself—it’s how well you manage the entire journey from concept to production. Welcome to Application Lifecycle Management (ALM), where strategic planning meets technical execution to transform how organizations deliver software. What is Application Lifecycle Management? First thing to remember, Application Lifecycle Management is the comprehensive approach to managing software applications throughout their entire existence—from initial planning and development through deployment, maintenance, and eventual retirement. Unlike traditional project management that focuses on discrete phases, ALM creates a continuous framework that connects people, processes, and tools across the entire software lifecycle. In other words, think of ALM as the orchestration layer that ensures every stage of your application’s journey is coordinated, traceable, and optimized for success. The Five Pillars of Effective ALM Think of ALM like planning and maintaining a well-run building: before construction begins, you need a clear blueprint, the right materials, inspections along the way, a reliable opening day, and ongoing maintenance to keep everything working as intended. Each pillar plays a similar role in the software lifecycle, helping teams move from an idea to a stable, useful application with fewer surprises. Requirements management sets the blueprint, development and version control organize the build, testing verifies the work, deployment brings it safely into use, and operations keeps it improving over time. Together, these pillars create the structure that turns software delivery from a risky handoff into a coordinated, repeatable process. 1. Requirements Management Every successful application begins with clear, well-documented requirements. This phase involves: Stakeholder collaboration to capture business needs and user expectations Requirements traceability to ensure nothing gets lost in translation Change management to handle evolving needs without derailing progress The key is creating a living requirements document that evolves with your project while maintaining clear connections between business objectives and technical implementation. 2. Development and Version Control Modern development demands more than just writing code—it requires structured collaboration and continuous integration: Version control systems (like Git) to track every change and enable team collaboration Branching strategies that support parallel development without conflicts Code reviews and quality gates to maintain standards throughout development This is where DevOps principles shine, enabling teams to work collaboratively while maintaining code quality and consistency. 3. Testing and Quality Assurance Quality can’t be an afterthought. Effective ALM integrates testing throughout the development process: Automated testing that runs with every code commit Continuous testing across unit, integration, and system levels Performance and security validation before production deployment By shifting testing left in the development cycle, organizations catch issues early when they’re easier and less expensive to fix. 4. Deployment and Release Management Deployment is where planning meets reality. Modern ALM leverages automation to ensure reliable, repeatable releases: CI/CD pipelines that automate build, test, and deployment processes Environment management ensuring consistency from development through production Rollback capabilities for quick recovery if issues arise The goal is making deployment a non-event—predictable, automated, and low-risk. 5. Operations and Continuous Improvement The lifecycle doesn’t end at deployment. Effective ALM includes: Monitoring and analytics to track application performance and user experience Incident response procedures for quick issue resolution Feedback loops that inform future development cycles This continuous improvement mindset ensures applications evolve to meet changing needs while maintaining stability and performance. The ALM Technology Stack Successful ALM implementation requires the right tools working together seamlessly: Project Management: Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms for tracking work and requirements to help teams plan, prioritize, and monitor progress Version Control: Source code management systems that track changes, support collaboration, and maintain a reliable history of development work CI/CD Tools : Automation platforms that streamline building, testing, and deploying applications across environments Testing Frameworks: Automated testing tools integrated into your pipeline Monitoring Solutions: Application performance monitoring and logging platforms The key is integration—these tools should work together to provide visibility and traceability across the entire lifecycle. Common ALM Challenges and Solutions Organizations implementing Application Lifecycle Management often encounter three fundamental challenges that can derail even the most well-intentioned initiatives. The first and perhaps most pervasive issue is siloed teams and processes. When development, operations, and security teams work in isolation, communication breaks down, handoffs become friction points, and the seamless flow that ALM promises becomes impossible to achieve. The solution lies in implementing collaborative practices that actively break down these barriers. By using shared tools, establishing common goals, and creating cross-functional teams, organizations can encourage the kind of collaboration that transforms ALM from a theoretical framework into a practical reality. The second major challenge involves manual, error-prone processes that plague traditional software delivery. When teams rely on manual testing, deployment checklists, and human intervention at critical junctures, mistakes become inevitable. These errors not only slow down delivery but also introduce risks that can impact production systems. The answer is embracing automation wherever possible. From automated testing that runs with every code commit to deployment pipelines that eliminate manual steps, automation reduces human error, increases consistency, and frees teams to focus on higher-value activities that require human creativity and judgment. The third challenge is lack of visibility across the application lifecycle. When teams can’t see what’s happening in real-time—whether it’s development progress, application health, or business outcomes—they’re essentially flying blind. This opacity leads to delayed problem detection, poor decision-making, and missed opportunities for improvement. Implementing comprehensive monitoring and reporting that provides real-time insights transforms this situation. When everyone can see application health metrics, development progress, and how technical decisions impact business outcomes, teams can respond quickly to issues and make informed decisions that drive success. Best Practices for ALM Success Success in Application Lifecycle Management doesn’t happen by accident—it requires deliberate practices that create the foundation for sustainable improvement. The journey begins with clear governance. Organizations must establish policies, procedures, and standards that guide decision-making throughout the lifecycle. This governance framework shouldn’t be bureaucratic overhead; rather, it should provide the guardrails that enable teams to move quickly while maintaining quality and compliance. When everyone understands the rules of the road, they can navigate confidently without constant oversight. Automation stands as another cornerstone of ALM success. By automating repetitive tasks—from code compilation and testing to deployment and monitoring—organizations improve both consistency and efficiency. Automation doesn’t replace human expertise; it amplifies it by handling the routine work that computers do better than people, allowing talented professionals to focus on problems that require creativity, judgment, and strategic thinking. Equally important is fostering genuine collaboration. This means creating environments where developers, operations teams, security professionals, and business stakeholders work together seamlessly rather than throwing work over walls to the next group. Collaboration requires more than just good intentions—it demands shared tools, common vocabularies, and organizational structures that reward teamwork over individual heroics. Additionally, measurement provides the feedback loop that drives continuous improvement. Organizations should track metrics that provide actionable insights: deployment frequency shows how often you deliver value, lead time reveals how quickly you respond to opportunities, change failure rate indicates quality, and mean time to recovery demonstrates resilience. These metrics aren’t about creating pressure—they’re about creating visibility that enables improvement. Finally, successful ALM requires a commitment to iteration and improvement. Using retrospectives and feedback loops, teams should continuously refine their processes. What worked last quarter might not work next quarter as technology evolves, team composition changes, and business needs shift. The organizations that thrive are those that treat their ALM processes as living systems that evolve based on experience and learning. The Business Impact of Effective ALM When organizations implement comprehensive Application Lifecycle Management practices, the benefits extend far beyond the IT department to impact the entire business. Perhaps most visibly, effective ALM delivers faster time-to-market. Streamlined processes and automation reduce development cycles, enabling organizations to respond more quickly to market opportunities and competitive threats. In today’s fast-paced business environment, the ability to deliver new features and capabilities rapidly can mean the difference between leading the market and playing catch-up. Quality improvements: Integrated testing and quality gates help teams catch issues earlier in development, leading to more reliable software, better user experiences, fewer production incidents, and lower support costs. Risk reduction: Better lifecycle visibility and automated controls make deployment failures less common, giving organizations the confidence to release updates more frequently and consistently. Improved collaboration: Shared tools and processes align development, operations, and business stakeholders around common goals, reducing silos, speeding decisions, and creating smoother teamwork. Lower costs: Early issue detection, process efficiency, and automation reduce rework, manual effort, and expensive production fixes, creating savings while also improving quality and speed. At its core, effective ALM helps organizations turn software delivery into a more intentional, dependable business capability. Instead of treating each release as a separate push to the finish line, teams build a connected lifecycle that supports long-term adaptability and sustained value. That shift is what makes ALM more than a technical practice—it becomes a strategic advantage. Transform Your Application Lifecycle MicroHealth helps organizations implement comprehensive Application Lifecycle Management practices through our expertise in Agile project management, DevOps automation, cloud engineering, and systems integration. We provide strategic guidance, technical implementation, training programs, and ongoing support to ensure your organization successfully manages applications from concept through deployment and beyond. Our approach combines proven methodologies with modern tools and practices, enabling your teams to deliver high-quality software faster and more reliably. From establishing governance frameworks to implementing CI/CD pipelines, we partner with you throughout your ALM transformation journey. Ready to optimize your application lifecycle? Contact us to discuss your ALM challenges and discover how we can help your organization deliver software with greater speed, quality, and confidence. title: Best Klaviyo Alternatives for eCommerce Brands With a Mobile App
summary: Searching for Klaviyo alternatives for your eCommerce app? Compare platforms on mobile app marketing, from push notification services to OneSignal vs Klaviyo.
body_text: A shopper who abandons a cart on your website is one kind of lost sale. A shopper who ignores a push notification on their phone is a different one entirely… and increasingly the more expensive one to lose. When mobile app marketing is a real growth channel for your brand, an email-first platform comparison only tells you half the story. This guide helps you choose the right engagement platform for your primary customer channels, not to argue that every brand must replace Klaviyo. We'll cover the decision criteria to use, an at-a-glance comparison of the leading Klaviyo alternatives, a detailed "Klaviyo vs. OneSignal" analysis, implementation considerations, and a clear selection framework you can apply to your own stack. Why eCommerce brands with apps need a different evaluation lens Klaviyo built its reputation on eCommerce email and SMS lifecycle marketing, and it does that work well. When you add a mobile app to the picture, the questions change. You start caring about push delivery on iOS and Android, in-app messaging, deep links that open the right product screen, and real-time alerts triggered by events in your app. An evaluation focused only on email deliverability and campaign templates will miss those needs. The right lens starts from the channels and journeys your customers actually use, then works backward to the platform that supports them. Some teams find their current tool covers everything. Others discover their app has become central to retention, and their engagement infrastructure has not kept up. Throughout this article, we'll keep the focus on your problems and outcomes: engagement, retention, conversion, and long-term customer value. What a push notification provider adds to an eCommerce app stack What is a push notification provider? A push notification provider is a platform that enables messaging to your app or web audiences through permission-based channels. For eCommerce teams, that means reaching shoppers with timely, relevant messages on the devices where they browse and buy. A useful way to size up any provider is against six practical criteria: reliability, scalability, rich-content support, platform support, customizability, and cost. Each one maps to a real question. Will messages arrive on time at volume? Can you send rich media and interactive formats? Does it cover iOS, Android, and web? Can you shape the experience, and can you predict what it costs as you grow? Push connects directly to concrete eCommerce journeys: Cart and browse recovery Price-drop alerts Order-status updates Re-engagement of lapsed users App-install prompts Onboarding series These aren't hypothetical gains, either. Inspire Uplift saw a 6% increase in sales conversions within its first month on OneSignal, with 10% of its entire web push revenue coming from automated abandoned-cart alerts alone, per OneSignal's case study. Evino, meanwhile, sees roughly 8% of total app revenue driven directly by push. These are illustrative use cases. Not every platform supports every journey natively, which is exactly what your evaluation needs to confirm. Where push fits alongside email and SMS Push, email, and SMS each do a different job, and the strongest programs coordinate them. Two message types matter here. Marketing campaigns are scheduled or triggered sends aimed at engagement and conversion. Transactional alerts are real-time, event-driven messages such as an order shipping or a payment confirmation, usually fired through an event-triggered API call. Making that coordination work depends on a few building blocks: audience data that stays current, deep links that route a shopper to the exact product or screen, and cross-channel orchestration so a customer isn't hit with the same message three ways. It helps to understand how OneSignal models this. A User is an individual who can have one or more subscriptions to channels such as push, email, and SMS. A Subscription is the specific device or channel through which that User receives messages. That distinction, described in OneSignal's documentation, keeps a single shopper unified across every device and channel they use. How to evaluate Klaviyo alternatives for mobile app marketing Turn the six criteria into a working scorecard. For each one, know exactly what to validate during a trial or technical review. Evaluate delivery and experience quality Delivery reliability: Test opt-in prompts, permission flows, and actual delivery rates. A push notification service that quietly drops messages costs you the exact moments you're paying to reach. Scalability: Confirm the platform handles your peak send volumes, such as a flash sale or a product launch. Rich-content support: Check for images, buttons, carousels, and interactive formats that make a message worth tapping. Platform coverage: Verify native support for iOS, Android, and web push, not just one surface. Check data, developer, and operational fit Customization and personalization: Test segmentation controls and dynamic content against your real customer data. SDK availability for every platform you ship on. API-triggered notifications so an app event can fire a message in real time. Event and profile-data ingestion , identity resolution, and how the platform unifies a shopper across devices. Deep-link behavior , integrations with your commerce stack, reporting depth, and how marketers and developers share work. Label each capability as native, integration-enabled, or something to confirm during evaluation. That distinction prevents you from assuming a feature exists because a competitor's marketing page implies it. Model the cost of growth Skip guessing at a total. Instead, list the cost drivers and price them against your own numbers: Contact or profile volume Subscriber volume Message volume Channel-specific credits or fees Feature tiers Implementation effort Ongoing operational time The platform that looks cheapest at 5,000 contacts can flip once you add SMS credits or cross a subscriber threshold. Model growth, not just launch. Klaviyo alternatives at a glance for eCommerce apps Before the detailed reviews, here's a fast scan of the leading Klaviyo alternatives positioned by best-fit scenario rather than universal rank. The right pick depends heavily on why you're leaving. Omnisend is a Shopify-focused email and SMS replacement, Brevo suits teams that want send-volume pricing, Sendlane suits DTC email and SMS performance, and EngageLab fits broader multi-channel orchestration across email, SMS, WhatsApp, and push. Platform Best fit for Mobile and web messaging coverage Automation, data, and developer considerations Pricing or scaling consideration OneSignal Teams prioritizing mobile and web push alongside email, SMS, and in-app Mobile push, web push, in-app messaging, email, SMS, RCS, and Live Activities (native); see our guide on switching engagement platforms Journeys for cross-channel orchestration; REST API; unified User and Subscription data model Free Plan with unlimited mobile subscribers; Growth Plan from $19/month with channel-usage costs MoEngage App-led brands wanting analytics-driven cross-channel engagement App and web personalization, cross-channel marketing (native); real-time transactional alerts via a single API Data management, insights, migration support, Shopify-focused eCommerce solution Commercial terms provided by sales; validate in a review Brevo Teams wanting send-volume pricing and broad channel reach Web and mobile push, email, SMS, WhatsApp, live chat (native) Campaign automation; transactional messaging via SMTP relay and API; 150+ integrations Send-volume pricing model EngageLab Global, multi-channel lifecycle messaging Email, SMS, WhatsApp, app push, web push (native) Multi-channel orchestration; medium migration effort Usage-based or product pricing Customer.io Complex, event-driven segmentation and logic-heavy workflows Mobile push, in-app messaging, email, SMS (native) Event-driven segmentation, omnichannel Journeys; API noted as limited versus OneSignal per OneSignal's own comparison Basic plan pricing starts in the low hundreds per month, scaling with profile count; confirm current tiers with Customer.io Omnisend Shopify-centric email and SMS teams Email, SMS, web push (native); no native mobile app push SDK Automation depth is an evaluation item for eCommerce workflows Low to medium migration effort The right fit ultimately depends on which channels carry your business today, and which ones your app needs tomorrow. Klaviyo vs. OneSignal for eCommerce apps The OneSignal vs Klaviyo question comes up often, and the honest answer is that the two products solve different problems. Klaviyo is an email and SMS lifecycle marketing platform built for eCommerce, whereas OneSignal is a push notification delivery platform for web and mobile messaging, alongside cross-channel orchestration. Your choice depends on the primary problem your team needs to solve. Channel strategy and mobile engagement Klaviyo centers on eCommerce email and SMS, with revenue attribution and lifecycle automation tied to your store data. Its free plan supports up to 250 profiles, 500 emails per month, and $5 of mobile messages per month, and its listed highlights include reporting, basic segmentation, revenue attribution, drag-and-drop email editing, automations, and mobile app marketing. On G2, OneSignal edges out Klaviyo overall (4.7 vs. 4.6 stars) and leads more clearly on ease of use and quality of support, differences that tend to show up fastest for lean teams without a dedicated martech admin. OneSignal brings push, email , SMS, RCS, and in-app messaging together in one accessible platform built for teams that don't have a full martech stack to lean on. For a team whose app drives retention, that push-and-in-app foundation is the center of gravity rather than an add-on. Segmentation, automation, and audience data When a career or a product shifts a marketer from managing one email channel to owning an entire omnichannel journey, the gaps in an email-first tool start to show. That transition is exactly what we explore in I Loved My ESP. Then My Job Changed . The right choice follows from the journeys and surfaces your customers use. Who should choose which platform? There's no blanket winner. Klaviyo is the stronger fit when the primary need is eCommerce email and SMS, while a push-first or cross-channel platform warrants priority when app push, in-app messaging, and mobile Journeys are central to retention. When eCommerce email and SMS are the center of the strategy If your revenue comes mostly through email flows and SMS, and your app is a secondary surface, Klaviyo's eCommerce depth and revenue attribution make it a strong fit to evaluate. Consider a complementary stack when channels have distinct jobs Some brands run Klaviyo for email and SMS alongside a dedicated platform for web and mobile push, because the channels play distinct roles in a coordinated stack. That's a valid design, not a compromise. Match your scenario to a profile: Shopify-centric email and SMS team: Omnisend or Klaviyo. App-led retailer needing price-drop, order-status, and re-engagement messaging: OneSignal. Team with complex event data and heavy workflow logic: Customer.io.
